With his children and their companions safe and with Phyra consolidating their plans Hom decided that now would be the opportune time to observe some of the races and creations that had risen in his absence. In his garden, reclining against the base of a great tree Hom allowed his consciousness to branch out, touching and sensing with endless fingers the many forms of life that had now come to reside on Gaea.

Far to the west, beyond the forest he had claimed for his own, a great titan sat awaiting command, a creature of the divine and no doubt the servant of one God or another its purpose undetermined.

Beneath the Sea he found the Naga, just as tempest had made them, untouched by the turmoil of the surface and their servants, sired from what had once been one of his children. The Naga, Hom thought were perhaps the most bizarre of the God's creations for though they were intelligent they lacked soul, the vital spark handed down by Yuna to all living peoples on Gaea, all that is, it would seem, except for the Naga. Their servants had also remained much as they were though now a spark of greatness dwelled within them, a spark which ignited would allow them to ascend to a greatness all their own. Wondering if it was possible to nurture this spark without interfering too greatly, Hom found his mind drawn to a single Lot'dy, far from home and within the city that had born the brunt of Phyra's wrath.

Within the City Hom was surprised to discover a plethora of races living alongside one another, Large men of metal, children of Yuna far from the tree of life and stranger yet a soul baring race made from shadow. Who could have created such an unusual race Hom mused, perhaps Umbralocht had given life to the shadows as agents of change or Tymoro as an act of punishment against the children of his compatriots. Never the less the race appeared to have prospered greatly.

Observing the race of shadows an idea flittered in Hom's mind, fleeting and farcical "Suppose a Naga, soul less but with body was merged with that of the Shadows who had soul but lacked body. What power would this new creature have? Would they prosper as the shadows have or regress to the brutality of the Naga? Questions for other times and other Gods.

To the North Hom found that Tymoro too had sown the seeds of civilization, his children now diligently working within the bowels of a mountain on projects yet to be realised. The proximity of the multi-armed engineers to the children of Phyra surprised the God (which seemed to be happening a lot of late) for the two Gods had often been at odds in ages gone by.

Last Hom returned to the forest where his temple lay in disarray, the doors felled by time, a wall collapsed by the shaking of the earth and the main hallway occupied by great thorned vines. "So, Zille has paid a visit I see" Hom smiled to himself as he bade the vines to recede and began to rebuild. Gathering the ashes of Mara, his once great queen, Hom bore her back from death with a breath. With her purpose served she would become the first to reside in his Garden, a daughter raised up to claim her crown and guard over the Heart of Gaea.

With his temple made whole and the world observed Hom withdrew his tendrils and sat, awaiting the next action of his brethren.

Denver won the Super Bowl via a physical, tough defense that played [kicking and screaming](http://www.milehighreport.com/2015/1/13/7539811/john-elway-was-frustrated-that-broncos-didnt-go-down-kicking-and) built after John Elway was pissed off at his team being pushed around in SB 48 and the following post season.

That defense was brilliant enough to earn discussion as to where they rank among top all time defenses, especially considering how mediocre (at best) their offense was (see the current thread "Can you think of a QB who had a worse year than Peyton Manning just had -- and won the Super Bowl?"). But numbers grinders say they're good, but [not ridiculously great](http://ftw.usatoday.com/2016/02/proof-that-the-broncos-put-together-one-of-the-greatest-nfl-defenses-of-all-time).

What these stat grinders fail to account for though is the situations the Denver D was put in. How well an offense plays is key to defensive statistical performance. It's common sense: a defense that has no offensive support will tire from being on the field too long, an offense that turns the ball over deep in its own territory doesn't set up its defense for success, etc and so forth. So let's compare the 2015-16 Broncos Squad to some memorable defenses from the past:

TEAM Offensive Ranking

2015 Broncos 16

2013 Seahwaks 9

2002 Bucs 18

2000 Ravens 14

1985 Bears 2

So Denver is in the lower side of offensive support of recent "all time" defenses, which helps their case but still isn't the complete story:

TEAM Total Offensive Give Aways

2015 Broncos 31

2013 Seahwaks 19

2002 Bucs 21

2000 Ravens 26

1985 Bears 31

So the Denver offense put the D in trouble a lot in a league that loves O. What does this all mean? The Denver D not only received minimal support in total offense but was the most put on the spot defense via turnovers in modern NFL history, and still got the job done. Moreover let's look at some playoff stats:

When it was win or go home time the 'Co's were at their best. The Broncos faced three likely future HOFers in a row and shut them all down (Brady a sure first ballot, Big Ben a probably, and Cam if he keeps current production up over a career):

The reigning MVP went 18/41 for 265, 6.5 per, no TDs and a pick. Tom "maybe GOAT" Brady went 27-of-56, 310 YDS, 1 TD, 2 INT, Big "two SBs" Roeth went 24/31 for no TDs.

In three *playoff* games this D gave up only a roughly 60% completion rate to three of the top QBs in the league, and a three to one pick to TD ratio. This isn't considering Von's SB strip sack et al...or the modern rules that favor offense. considering how little support they got and the bad positions they were constantly put i the 2015 Denver D deserves to be mentioned in the all time conversation.
A deeper look at stats suggests the SB winning Denver Defense is even better than you think
